canonical_seed.student_text: A lab group wants to compare the average speeds of two wind-up cars without assuming either car moves uniformly. Describe what distance and elapsed-time measurements they should collect, how the relationship average speed = distance/time would be used, and what a difference in the ratios would mean.

\(v_{avg}=\frac{d}{t}\)

canonical_seed.student_text: A hockey puck slides across very smooth ice. Ignore small resistance. If no net force acts, what motion should continue?
canonical_seed.student_html:
A hockey puck slides across very smooth ice. Ignore small resistance. If no net force acts, what motion should continue?

  1. Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.
  2. It must gradually stop because motion always requires a forward net force.
  3. A force called inertia keeps pushing it in its current direction.
  4. Zero net force means no individual forces can be acting.

choices.text: Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.
It must gradually stop because motion always requires a forward net force.
A force called inertia keeps pushing it in its current direction.
Zero net force means no individual forces can be acting.

canonical_seed.answer: Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no acceleration: rest remains rest, and constant straight-line velocity remains unchanged.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no acceleration: rest remains rest, and constant straight-line velocity remains unchanged.

  2. Inertia is a property of matter, not an extra force acting on the object.
  3. Inertia is a hidden force that always points in the direction of motion.
  4. Inertia is the same thing as net force.

choices.text: Inertia exists only when an object is at rest.
Inertia is a property of matter, not an extra force acting on the object.
Inertia is a hidden force that always points in the direction of motion.
Inertia is the same thing as net force.

canonical_seed.solution_text: The claim is incorrect. Inertia is a property of matter describing resistance to a change in velocity; it is not an additional force. Force arrows should represent actual interactions on the object.

canonical_seed.solution_text: Zero net force is the vector sum of forces being zero; it is not the absence of all individual forces.

  3. The object is at rest only because no forces act on it.
  4. The upward force is inertia rather than an interaction force.

The object may be at rest because nonzero forces balance to zero net force.
The object is at rest only because no forces act on it.
The upward force is inertia rather than an interaction force.

canonical_seed.solution_text: Rest does not imply the absence of forces. Multiple forces can act and balance so their vector sum is zero.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Rest does not imply the absence of forces. Multiple forces can act and balance so their vector sum is zero.

canonical_seed.student_text: Draw a force diagram for the crate in this situation: a crate pushed to the right across a level floor while it speeds up. Include only forces acting on the crate, with appropriate directions and labels.

canonical_seed.student_text: Use the arrow magnitudes in the supplied force diagram rather than the object’s motion. Which statement correctly classifies the force balance?
canonical_seed.student_html:
Use the arrow magnitudes in the supplied force diagram rather than the object’s motion. Which statement correctly classifies the force balance?

  1. unbalanced only because the object is moving
  2. no forces act because a force diagram cannot show balanced forces
  3. unbalanced; the opposing arrows do not represent equal force magnitudes, so the net force is nonzero
  4. balanced because any two opposite arrows always cancel even if their lengths differ

choices.text: unbalanced only because the object is moving
no forces act because a force diagram cannot show balanced forces
unbalanced; the opposing arrows do not represent equal force magnitudes, so the net force is nonzero
balanced because any two opposite arrows always cancel even if their lengths differ

canonical_seed.answer: unbalanced; the opposing arrows do not represent equal force magnitudes, so the net force is nonzero
canonical_seed.solution_text: Balanced forces have a zero vector sum; unequal opposing forces give a nonzero net force.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Balanced forces have a zero vector sum; unequal opposing forces give a nonzero net force.

canonical_seed.student_text: A classmate says the longest visible arrow is the object’s motion arrow. Use the supplied force model to choose the correction that treats every arrow as an interaction force.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A classmate says the longest visible arrow is the object’s motion arrow. Use the supplied force model to choose the correction that treats every arrow as an interaction force.

  1. Use the vector sum of the force arrows: zero net force means no acceleration; a nonzero net force means the velocity changes in the net-force direction.
  2. If the object is moving right, the net force must always point right.
  3. Balanced forces disappear from the diagram.
  4. The longest arrow represents the object’s velocity rather than a force.

choices.text: Use the vector sum of the force arrows: zero net force means no acceleration; a nonzero net force means the velocity changes in the net-force direction.
If the object is moving right, the net force must always point right.
Balanced forces disappear from the diagram.
The longest arrow represents the object’s velocity rather than a force.

canonical_seed.answer: Use the vector sum of the force arrows: zero net force means no acceleration; a nonzero net force means the velocity changes in the net-force direction.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Net force determines acceleration/change in velocity. Motion direction by itself does not determine net-force direction.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Net force determines acceleration/change in velocity. Motion direction by itself does not determine net-force direction.

canonical_seed.student_text: Audit the supplied force model against a zero-net-force explanation. Identify one arrow or balance feature that supports or contradicts the claim, then write the corrected motion prediction.
canonical_seed.student_html: Audit the supplied force model against a zero-net-force explanation. Identify one arrow or balance feature that supports or contradicts the claim, then write the corrected motion prediction.
canonical_seed.answer: A correct critique compares the motion claim with the force vector sum. If the forces balance, net force is zero and velocity stays constant; if they do not balance, the velocity changes in the direction of the net force. Revise any statement that treats motion direction as a force or says balanced forces vanish.
